name: side-panel
title: Side Panel
description: A non-modal inspector beside a list: a named complementary region, Escape closes it and returns focus to the row, shortcuts declared inside run while it is open, and on narrow screens it stacks below the list, overlays it or opens as a bottom sheet.
docs: `<SidePanel open onOpenChange title description actions returnFocus>` renders nothing while closed. Lay it out beside the list in a flex row (`--side-panel-width`, 24rem by default). `actions` (a status pill, small buttons) sit beside the title until the title would get narrower than `--card-heading-basis` (11rem), then wrap below it, as `CardHeader`'s do; the close button keeps its corner. `narrow` sets what happens at the `narrow:` breakpoint (760px and below): `"stack"` (default) keeps it in the page flow, full width, and makes its flex parent wrap so it goes below the list; `"overlay"` covers its positioned parent, as it always did before; `"sheet"` opens it as a modal bottom `Drawer` that takes focus and returns it to `returnFocus()` on close. `stack` is the default because it is the only mode that neither hides the page nor traps focus, so a panel that is open on load still leaves the list readable and reachable. Use `overlay` to show the panel instead of the list (a tall scroller in a bounded column, as the `inbox` block does), and `sheet` for a detail that should read as a step away from the list. Escape anywhere on the page closes it (a modal above it gets Escape first), and focus that was inside it, or lost to the body, moves to `returnFocus()`. It is a `ShortcutScope` that is active while open (`scope`, `scopeLabel` for the `ShortcutsDialog`), so `Button shortcut="u"` inside it works while focus stays in the list. `labels={{ close }}` names the close button.
